9. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners laid much emphasis on the Commissioner's report urging that a commissioner was appointed to determine the possession of the plaintiff-petitioners. It is settled law that evidence on the point of a possession is to be assessed not by the learned Advocate Commissioner but on the basis of evidence to be adduced by the parties during trial. It may be mentioned here that previous suit (OC suit No. 65 or 1970) filed by the plaintiff-petitioner on the basis of added of contract ended in dismissal on contest. So the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that the case is hit by principle of res judicata inasmuch as the earlier suit referred to above was based on same cause of action between the same parties in respect of the same subject matter. The object of the principle of res judicata as suggested by the expression itself is that finality should impart to judicial decision and if a case is adjudicated, it may not be reopened so as to be adjudicated again. Thus a suit between same parties in relation to same cause of action for same relief is barred by res judicata Fundamental principle of res judicate is that a question must be finally decided once and for all by a competent Court and after it is so decided further litigation about it should be concluded for ever between the parties. The maxim is that, "no one shall be vexed twice over the same matter," which' pre-supposes that the issue has been fairly and finally tried and decided it) a former suit, which was independent of the proceedings in which the same matter is again in dispute. In other words, (i) once a matter between the parties to a suit or proceeding is decided and the decision has become final (ii) no appeal was taken or (iii) if taken it was dismissed, none of the parties shall be allowed to canvass the same matter again in a subsequent suit or proceedings between the same parties. As a result of the application of this principle as embodied in s. 11 of the CPC all future litigations at any length between the parties must proceed on the presumption of correctness of the previous decision. Thus where in .a previous suit the pica of validity of decree has already been taken and decided, then subsequent suit on the basis of the same pica will be barred by res Judicata.
